articles.originalTitle: Israeli election: Netanyahu, main rival fall short of majority after all votes counted
articles.originalText: With all the votes counted, the pro-Netanyahu bloc finished ahead of Gadi Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu bloc. But as neither grouping won a majority, tough coalition talks are ahead. Follow DW.
articles.originalFullText:
What you need to know

- Israel's election turnout was the highest in decades

- The final vote count showed Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc finished with 53 seats

- The anti-Netanyahu bloc, led by Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, claimed 48 seats

- At least 61 seats are needed to form a secure majority

- As neither party won an outright majority, difficult coalition talks are expected in the weeks ahead

Follow below for all the latest on the Israeli election.

Tricky task of forming a working coalition begins

Ahead of the election, two clear coalitions had formed. On the one side, the ruling coalition of right-wing, far-right and religious parties centered around Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party.

On the other side was the anti-Netanyahu bloc, made up of a coalition of right-wing, centrist and liberal parties whose unifying principle was to oust Netanyahu from power.

However, neither of these blocs was able to secure a majority of seats, meaning a simple path to forming a government is off the table.

The task of figuring out a new working coalition is now beginning, with the question of whether the two Arab-Israeli lists, which together secured an unprecedented 19 seats, may form part of a future government or at least provide some form of support.

Yair Golan, chairman of the left-liberal Democrats, said he had met with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, former Prime Minister Yair Lapid and Mansur Abbas, head of the Arab Ra'am party.

He has called for discussions with the Arab-led parties, saying after his meeting with Eisenkot that "the rescue of Israel is at stake," in a post on X.

It remains to be seen if the right-wing factions of Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu bloc would ultimately entertain the possibility of working with the Arab-led parties.

Another option that has been aired is the possibility of a unity government including both Netanyahu and Eisenkot, but such a move may be similarly distasteful for moderate voters.

Final count released

The final count of ballots from Tuesday's vote has been released by Israel's Central Election Committee.

Netanyahu's bloc with a total of 53 seats

- Likud - 27

- UTJ - 7

- Otzma Yehudit - 7

- Shas - 6

- RZP - 6

Eisenkot's bloc with a total of 48 seats

- Yashar - 21

- B'Yachad - 12

- The Democrats - 8

- Yisrael Beytenu - 7

The Arab Israeli parties with a total of 19 seats

- Joint List - 11

- Ra'am - 8

READ: Authorities dispute Netanyahu’s fraud claims

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud claims large-scale foreign involvement in the elections led by Qatar and Turkey, with Israel’s authorities so far refuting the claims.

Israeli police said there is no evidence to support Likud's claims, neither "investigative” nor "informative.”

A high-ranking Central Election Committee official, too, denied the allegations.

Read more in depth coverage of that story, right here.

Israel elections: Where things stand on Thursday afternoon

With the final tally of votes in Israel's high-stakes parliamentary elections expected on Thursday evening, we take a look at today's events thus far.

- Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party doubled down on allegations that the election has been stolen by Arab parties.

- Netanyahu said that evidence would be handed to police, Shin Bet and the Central Elections Committee.

- Netanyahu also referred to statements about the "involvement of foreign entities that interfered and bribed voters in favor of Arab parties," saying they were "an unprecedented shock."

- Netanyahu's main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, said political actors should not "exploit the information" that had yet to be clarified "in order undermine the official results."

- Qatar meanwhile, has denied any involvement in such allegations: "We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome," it said, adding it is accused of buying off the Arab vote.

- Qatar’s foreign minister spokesman Majed Al Ansari spoke of "accusations made by certain Israeli politicians" and said they had "launched yet another disinformation campaign aiming to drag Qatar into Israeli political disputes."

- Sami Abu Shehadeh, chair of one of the parties in the Arab-led Joint List, called the claims a new phase of "incitement" against Arab-led groups.

- The head of the Arab-led Ra'am party, Mansour Abbas, welcomed any investigation into election interference. He said his party had nothing to do with it.

- Israel's Central Elections Committee poured cold water on vote fraud allegeations saying "there is no basis."

- "The Knesset elections were conducted lawfully. The integrity of the elections at polling stations was rigorously safeguarded, and to the best of our knowledge, there is no basis for allegations of systematic violations of election integrity," The Times of Israel quoted acting Central Elections Committee director general Dean Livne as having written in a letter.

Netanyahu, Eisenkot blocs far from majority as count nears its end

With 89.8% of ballots counted, the bloc led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, compared with 48 seats for the anti-Netanyahu alliance led by former military commander Gadi Eisenkot, according to the Central Election Committee (CEC) as reported by the Times of Israel.

That leaves both blocs far short of the 61 seats needed for a majority.

The two majority Arab parties seem set to win 19 seats between them, a record tally that beats their previous high of 15 seats.

Netanyahu has ruled out working with the Arab parties to gain a majority, but there have been signs that some parties in Eisenkot's bloc might be open to the idea, though Eisenkot himself has also previously rejected it.

The absentee ballots — "double-envelope" votes — whose count began on Thursday are not expected to materially affect the final results, despite making up almost 10% of the overall vote.

Final tally underway, including 'double envelope' absentee ballots

The Central Elections Commission (CEC) has said that counting of so-called double envelope ballots began early Thursday morning, according to the Times of Israel.

Such ballots are cast mostly by soldiers, prisoners and diplomats stationed abroad, as well as others unable to vote at their assigned polling stations.

According to Israeli media, the CEC is reckoning with between 430,000 and 480,000 such ballots, lower than its previous prediction of some 600,000 but still representing just under 10% of votes cast.

This could theoretically still impact seat distribution to a considerable extent.

The Times of Israel also cited the CEC as saying that not all regular votes have been completely counted.

A full vote count is tentatively expected by Thursday afternoon, although the official finalized results will not be issued until November 4.

UN rights chief: Next government should 'change course massively'

The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, told reporters in New York that he hopes a new Israeli government will "change course massively" and respect international law.

"The message is: don't continue the current course of warfare where you think you are above international law, because I think that's what we have frankly seen in the current environment," Türk said, as relayed by the AFP news agency.

"Israel has its obligations under international law, international humanitarian law, international human rights law, and they need to respect them," he said. "And I hope that the next government will do precisely that and change course massively."

Türk also said in a statement on Monday that Israel's operation in recent days in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron raised serious concerns about "unnecessary and disproportionate" use of force.

He said that more than 2,000 people had been displaced, with homes and commercial property destroyed and free movement impeded by the lockdown.

"Collective punishment is a grave violation of international law," Türk said. "Threats to empty and erase entire neighborhoods also raise serious concerns of ethnic cleansing."

'Arab Israelis have trusted democracy,' Greens' Omid Nouripour tells DW

Omid Nouripour, one of the deputy speakers in Germany's Bundestag parliament, has told DW that the high turnout in Israel was a testament to the strength of the country's democracy.

"For now, of course, we do not know what the coalition-building will look like, but the people have put their trust in democracy," Nouripour said. "Above all, Arab Israelis have trusted democracy and gone to the polls in droves."

Speaking to DW's Rosalia Romaniec, as he accompanies German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier on his state visit to China, Nouripour also said that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's and other right-wing parties' religiously-charged campaign strategy appeared to have backfired.

"This big campaign from Netanyahu's camp, first and foremost against the Arab Israelis, has on the one hand mobilized people to such an extent that there is no longer a majority for this camp," he said.

Nouripour, a former Green party co-leader, has been a Bundestag member for 20 years. Born in Tehran, his family moved from Iran to Germany when he was a teenager.

WATCH: Early Israeli election results point to deadlock

Israel's election has produced no clear winner, leaving both Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot short of a path to power. Israel could now be facing weeks of political uncertainty.

IN DEPTH: What would a new Israeli government mean for Arab neighbors?

A new Israeli government is unlikely to bring big changes on controversial topics like Palestinian statehood and Israeli troops in Lebanon and Syria, experts say.

Some small positives may be possible though.

Read DW's full report on what might change for Arab countries after Israel's election.

GRAPHIC — Knesset seats by party, and by bloc

Election commission says almost half a million 'double envelope' ballots still to be counted

The Central Elections Commission (CEC) estimates that there are still between 430,000 and 480,000 so-called "double envelope" ballots to count, according to Israeli media.

These are cast primarily by soldiers, prisoners and diplomats stationed abroad, as well as others unable to vote at their designated polling stations.

This estimate is lower than the CEC's previous prediction of around 600,000 but it remains subject to change.

Such ballots are still being received and processed, and officials also have to double-check that the individuals sending them in have not also voted at a physical polling station on election day.

Because of these complications, they tend to be among the last votes to be counted.

A full vote count is tentatively expected by tomorrow afternoon, although the official finalized results will only follow on November 4.

If the CEC's estimated range is roughly correct, this group of ballots would equate to not very far shy of 10% of the total number of votes cast. As such, they have at least the theoretical potential to impact the seat distribution quite considerably.

President Herzog says it's imperative 'to avoid another round of elections'

President Isaac Herzog, who will have a key role in choosing someone to try to put together the next government, has urged all parties to "come with an open mind" when the time for negotiations comes.

"I will receive the official election results next week," Herzog said. "I wil then begin the process of the consultations here, hearing from each and every fraction, asking questions, and holding discussions."

Typically the president chooses the leader of the party with the most votes to try to form a government although he is not required to follow this convention. That nominee then has 42 days to try to set up a working coalition.

"One thing must be clear, and I said this before the elections too," Herzog said. "We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections. So I expect everyone who comes here to come with an open mind."

Between April 2019 and November 2022, Israel had five general elections in rather rapid succession amid similar difficulties either forming or maintaining coalition governments.

Situation barely moves as more than 80% of vote counted

Partial results published by the Central Elections Committee and reported by the Times of Israel newspaper showed the bloc led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on 54 seats, with 84.5% of votes counted.

The opposition bloc under Gadi Eisenkot of the centrist Yashar party was on 49 seats.

Neither bloc is set to receive the 61 seats need for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, making some form of coalition likely.

The Arab-led parties — the Joint List and the United Arab List, commonly known under its Hebrew name of Ra'am — have dropped to 17 seats.

The numbers are still likely to change, particularly after a record number of absentee votes are counted.

The full tally of those will possibly not be confirmed until Friday, according to the newspaper.

Arab list leader calls for Jewish-Arab partnership to oust Netanyahu

The leader of the far-left Joint List, one of Israel's Arab-majority lists, has called for a "genuine Jewish-Arab partnership" to help remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"Anyone who wants to offer a substantive and genuine alternative to Netanyahu's blood-soaked government will have to talk to us to secure the path to the change that the public in Israel longs for," Yousef Jabareen told Israeli media.

"We will know how to use our political strength to advance the values we believe in," Jabareen said.

"We are ready to pave the way for the replacement of the government of Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir and [Finance Minister Bezalel] Smotrich — and send them home."

After most votes have been counted from Tuesday's election, the conservative Islamist Ra'am party and the Joint List are projected to win a combined 19 seats in the 120-member Knesset.

As neither the pro-Netanyahu bloc nor the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot seem likely to win a majority, the Arab parties could play a key role in the formation of the next government.

Right-wing Jewish parties in Israel have traditionally refused to cooperate with Arab parties, and Netanyahu said on Wednesday doing so would be "treasonous."

However, at least one opposition party is open to the idea, with the leader of the left-leading Democrats, Yair Golan, saying Wednesday he supported bringing Arab-led parties into a coalition.

What you need to know

- Israel's election turnout was the highest in decades

- The final vote count showed Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc finished with 53 seats

- The anti-Netanyahu bloc, led by Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, claimed 48 seats

- At least 61 seats are needed to form a secure majority

- As neither party won an outright majority, difficult coalition talks are expected in the weeks ahead

Follow below for all the latest on the Israeli election.

Tricky task of forming a working coalition begins

Ahead of the election, two clear coalitions had formed. On the one side, the ruling coalition of right-wing, far-right and religious parties centered around Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party.

On the other side was the anti-Netanyahu bloc, made up of a coalition of right-wing, centrist and liberal parties whose unifying principle was to oust Netanyahu from power.

However, neither of these blocs was able to secure a majority of seats, meaning a simple path to forming a government is off the table.

The task of figuring out a new working coalition is now beginning, with the question of whether the two Arab-Israeli lists, which together secured an unprecedented 19 seats, may form part of a future government or at least provide some form of support.

Yair Golan, chairman of the left-liberal Democrats, said he had met with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, former Prime Minister Yair Lapid and Mansur Abbas, head of the Arab Ra'am party.

He has called for discussions with the Arab-led parties, saying after his meeting with Eisenkot that "the rescue of Israel is at stake," in a post on X.

It remains to be seen if the right-wing factions of Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu bloc would ultimately entertain the possibility of working with the Arab-led parties.

Another option that has been aired is the possibility of a unity government including both Netanyahu and Eisenkot, but such a move may be similarly distasteful for moderate voters.

Final count released

The final count of ballots from Tuesday's vote has been released by Israel's Central Election Committee.

Netanyahu's bloc with a total of 53 seats

- Likud - 27

- UTJ - 7

- Otzma Yehudit - 7

- Shas - 6

- RZP - 6

Eisenkot's bloc with a total of 48 seats

- Yashar - 21

- B'Yachad - 12

- The Democrats - 8

- Yisrael Beytenu - 7

The Arab Israeli parties with a total of 19 seats

- Joint List - 11

- Ra'am - 8

READ: Authorities dispute Netanyahu’s fraud claims

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud claims large-scale foreign involvement in the elections led by Qatar and Turkey, with Israel’s authorities so far refuting the claims.

Israeli police said there is no evidence to support Likud's claims, neither "investigative” nor "informative.”

A high-ranking Central Election Committee official, too, denied the allegations.

Read more in depth coverage of that story, right here.

Israel elections: Where things stand on Thursday afternoon

With the final tally of votes in Israel's high-stakes parliamentary elections expected on Thursday evening, we take a look at today's events thus far.

- Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party doubled down on allegations that the election has been stolen by Arab parties.

- Netanyahu said that evidence would be handed to police, Shin Bet and the Central Elections Committee.

- Netanyahu also referred to statements about the "involvement of foreign entities that interfered and bribed voters in favor of Arab parties," saying they were "an unprecedented shock."

- Netanyahu's main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, said political actors should not "exploit the information" that had yet to be clarified "in order undermine the official results."

- Qatar meanwhile, has denied any involvement in such allegations: "We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome," it said, adding it is accused of buying off the Arab vote.

- Qatar’s foreign minister spokesman Majed Al Ansari spoke of "accusations made by certain Israeli politicians" and said they had "launched yet another disinformation campaign aiming to drag Qatar into Israeli political disputes."

- Sami Abu Shehadeh, chair of one of the parties in the Arab-led Joint List, called the claims a new phase of "incitement" against Arab-led groups.

- The head of the Arab-led Ra'am party, Mansour Abbas, welcomed any investigation into election interference. He said his party had nothing to do with it.

- Israel's Central Elections Committee poured cold water on vote fraud allegeations saying "there is no basis."

- "The Knesset elections were conducted lawfully. The integrity of the elections at polling stations was rigorously safeguarded, and to the best of our knowledge, there is no basis for allegations of systematic violations of election integrity," The Times of Israel quoted acting Central Elections Committee director general Dean Livne as having written in a letter.

Netanyahu, Eisenkot blocs far from majority as count nears its end

With 89.8% of ballots counted, the bloc led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, compared with 48 seats for the anti-Netanyahu alliance led by former military commander Gadi Eisenkot, according to the Central Election Committee (CEC) as reported by the Times of Israel.

That leaves both blocs far short of the 61 seats needed for a majority.

The two majority Arab parties seem set to win 19 seats between them, a record tally that beats their previous high of 15 seats.

Netanyahu has ruled out working with the Arab parties to gain a majority, but there have been signs that some parties in Eisenkot's bloc might be open to the idea, though Eisenkot himself has also previously rejected it.

The absentee ballots — "double-envelope" votes — whose count began on Thursday are not expected to materially affect the final results, despite making up almost 10% of the overall vote.

Final tally underway, including 'double envelope' absentee ballots

The Central Elections Commission (CEC) has said that counting of so-called double envelope ballots began early Thursday morning, according to the Times of Israel.

Such ballots are cast mostly by soldiers, prisoners and diplomats stationed abroad, as well as others unable to vote at their assigned polling stations.

According to Israeli media, the CEC is reckoning with between 430,000 and 480,000 such ballots, lower than its previous prediction of some 600,000 but still representing just under 10% of votes cast.

This could theoretically still impact seat distribution to a considerable extent.

The Times of Israel also cited the CEC as saying that not all regular votes have been completely counted.

A full vote count is tentatively expected by Thursday afternoon, although the official finalized results will not be issued until November 4.

UN rights chief: Next government should 'change course massively'

The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, told reporters in New York that he hopes a new Israeli government will "change course massively" and respect international law.

"The message is: don't continue the current course of warfare where you think you are above international law, because I think that's what we have frankly seen in the current environment," Türk said, as relayed by the AFP news agency.

"Israel has its obligations under international law, international humanitarian law, international human rights law, and they need to respect them," he said. "And I hope that the next government will do precisely that and change course massively."

Türk also said in a statement on Monday that Israel's operation in recent days in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron raised serious concerns about "unnecessary and disproportionate" use of force.

He said that more than 2,000 people had been displaced, with homes and commercial property destroyed and free movement impeded by the lockdown.

"Collective punishment is a grave violation of international law," Türk said. "Threats to empty and erase entire neighborhoods also raise serious concerns of ethnic cleansing."

'Arab Israelis have trusted democracy,' Greens' Omid Nouripour tells DW

Omid Nouripour, one of the deputy speakers in Germany's Bundestag parliament, has told DW that the high turnout in Israel was a testament to the strength of the country's democracy.

"For now, of course, we do not know what the coalition-building will look like, but the people have put their trust in democracy," Nouripour said. "Above all, Arab Israelis have trusted democracy and gone to the polls in droves."

Speaking to DW's Rosalia Romaniec, as he accompanies German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier on his state visit to China, Nouripour also said that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's and other right-wing parties' religiously-charged campaign strategy appeared to have backfired.

"This big campaign from Netanyahu's camp, first and foremost against the Arab Israelis, has on the one hand mobilized people to such an extent that there is no longer a majority for this camp," he said.

Nouripour, a former Green party co-leader, has been a Bundestag member for 20 years. Born in Tehran, his family moved from Iran to Germany when he was a teenager.

WATCH: Early Israeli election results point to deadlock

Israel's election has produced no clear winner, leaving both Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot short of a path to power. Israel could now be facing weeks of political uncertainty.

IN DEPTH: What would a new Israeli government mean for Arab neighbors?

A new Israeli government is unlikely to bring big changes on controversial topics like Palestinian statehood and Israeli troops in Lebanon and Syria, experts say.

Some small positives may be possible though.

Read DW's full report on what might change for Arab countries after Israel's election.

articles.originalTitle: Kim urges drone dominance as North Korea fires missiles and rockets
articles.originalText: According to KCNA, Kim said that pursuing superiority in drone technology was "an indispensable option" given the changing nature of modern warfare.
articles.originalFullText:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for his country to seize “absolute superiority” in drone technology as he attended an exhibition and demonstration of unmanned aeronautical technology, state media KCNA reported on Friday.

The firepower demonstration following the exhibition involved tactical suicide attack drones, tactical cruise missiles, multipurpose drones and a battalion of 600 mm multiple rocket launchers, KCNA said.

The display highlighted Kim’s push to modernize North Korea’s armed forces by using drones and artificial intelligence as Pyongyang draws lessons from its forces’ experience in Russia’s war against Ukraine and from other global conflicts.
articles.title: Ким призывает к доминированию беспилотников, поскольку Северная Корея запускает ракеты и ракеты
articles.text: Ким сказал, что стремление к превосходству в технологии беспилотных летательных аппаратов является «незаменимым вариантом», учитывая меняющийся характер современной войны.
articles.fullText:
Северокорейский лидер Ким Чен Ын Ун призвал свою страну захватить «абсолютное превосходство» в технологии беспилотных летательных аппаратов, когда он присутствовал на выставке и демонстрации беспилотных авиационных технологий, сообщили государственные СМИ KCNA в пятницу.

Демонстрация огневой мощи по итогам выставки включала тактические беспилотники-самоубийцы, тактические крылатые ракеты, многоцелевые беспилотники и батальон 600-мм реактивных систем залпового огня.

На выставке было показано стремление Кима модернизировать вооруженные силы Северной Кореи с помощью беспилотников и искусственного интеллекта, поскольку Пхеньян извлекает уроки из опыта своих сил в войне России против Украины и других глобальных конфликтов.

articles.originalFullText:
Уполномоченная по правам человека Яна Лантратова сообщила о смерти двух человек в Алешках Херсонской области при разминировании территории для проезда гуманитарной миссии. Слова Лантратовой приводит ТАСС.

По словам омбудсмена, одной из жертв стал сапер. «Мы выражаем соболезнования родным и близким», — заявила она.

При этом Лантратова подчеркнула, что Украина и Россия соблюдают взятые на себя обязательства.

О локальном перемирии в Алешках Россия и Украина при посредничестве первой леди США Мелании Трамп договорились 23 октября. Оно было необходимо, чтобы обеспечить доставку гуманитарной помощи и подготовить эвакуацию мирных граждан.

articles.originalTitle: Папа Римский решил проголосовать на выборах в США
articles.originalText: Папа Римский Лев XIV, имеющий регистрацию избирателя в американском штате Иллинойс, запросил бюллетень для голосования по почте на промежуточных выборах в Конгресс США. Об этом сообщила телеканал NBC News
articles.originalFullText:
Папа Римский Лев XIV, имеющий регистрацию избирателя в американском штате Иллинойс, запросил бюллетень для голосования по почте на промежуточных выборах в Конгресс США. Об этом сообщила телеканал NBC News.

Глава католической церкви подал запрос на получение бюллетеня 3 октября, подтвердила изданию руководитель аппарата клерка округа Уилл-Каунти Ким Фладхаммер.

«Канцелярия клерка пока не получила заполненный бюллетень от понтифика», — говорится в материале NBC News.

Авторы материала отмечают, что Лев XIV, при рождении получивший имя Роберт Фрэнсис Превост, может стать первым папой римским, принявшим участие в выборах в США. Он стал первым американцем на папском престоле в мае 2025 года.

19 октября президент России Владимир Путин и Папа Римский Лев XIV в ходе телефонного разговора обсудили ситуацию в Алешках. Российский лидер поблагодарил понтифика за готовность внести вклад в урегулирование конфликта на Украине и те усилия, которые Святой престол предпринимает на гуманитарном направлении.

articles.originalTitle: Brazil’s Lula forced into tricky top court reform by unrestrained judge
articles.originalText: A powerful justice has become a liability for the reelected president just as he prepares for a new term promising to heal the country's divisions.
articles.originalFullText:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has a big Supreme Court problem. Its name is Alexandre de Moraes.

The powerful justice, once celebrated for protecting Brazilian democracy from Jair Bolsonaro’s attempts to undermine it, has become a liability for the reelected president just as he prepares for a new term promising to heal the country’s deep divisions.

Barely hours after Lula defeated Bolsonaro’s son Flavio in Sunday’s presidential runoff, Moraes ordered the losing candidate to surrender his passports, citing concerns that he might flee the country as multiple criminal investigations close in on him.
articles.title: Бразильская Лула была вынуждена провести сложную реформу высшего суда безудержным судьей
articles.text: Мощное правосудие стало ответственностью для переизбранного президента, когда он готовится к новому сроку, обещая исцелить разногласия в стране.
articles.fullText:
Президент Бразилии Луис Инасиу Лула да Силва столкнулся с серьезной проблемой в Верховном суде. Его зовут Александр де Мораес.

Мощное правосудие, когда-то прославленное за защиту бразильской демократии от попыток Жаира Болсонару подорвать ее, стало ответственностью для переизбранного президента, так же как он готовится к новому сроку, обещая исцелить глубокие разногласия в стране.

Спустя всего несколько часов после того, как Лула победил сына Болсонару Флавио во втором туре президентских выборов, Мораес приказал проигравшему кандидату сдать свои паспорта, сославшись на опасения, что он может покинуть страну, поскольку многочисленные уголовные расследования закрываются на него.

articles.originalTitle: VOX POPULI: Analog makes a comeback after a multitude of cyberattacks
articles.originalText: Seven years ago during a trip to northern Europe, I was struck by how thoroughly cashless payments had taken hold. It was almost impossible to pay for goods and services with banknotes and coins. And it was not just shopping. Public toilets often charged a fee, and their doors would not open until a credit card had been swiped. The trip offered a disquieting glimpse of a digitalized society seemingly hostile to an analog way of life—one in which, without a card, even answering the call of nature could become an ordeal.
articles.originalFullText:
Vox Populi, Vox Dei is a daily column that runs on Page 1 of The Asahi Shimbun.

October 30, 2026 at 14:13 JST

A customer makes a cashless payment at a vending machine. (Asahi Shimbun file photo)

Seven years ago during a trip to northern Europe, I was struck by how thoroughly cashless payments had taken hold. It was almost impossible to pay for goods and services with banknotes and coins.

And it was not just shopping. Public toilets often charged a fee, and their doors would not open until a credit card had been swiped.

The trip offered a disquieting glimpse of a digitalized society seemingly hostile to an analog way of life—one in which, without a card, even answering the call of nature could become an ordeal.

Sweden, which once appeared to be heading inexorably toward a cashless future, began to change course following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Concerned about the threat of Russian cyberattacks, Swedish authorities began urging people to keep cash on hand and retain the ability to use it in everyday transactions.

Norway has taken a similar path. Its government has urged people to keep cash at home, while legislation provides for fines against retailers that refuse to accept it. It is an unexpected return to the analog world.

In Japan, too, where new cases of damage from cyberattacks seem to emerge almost daily, a technology once thought destined for the dustbin of history is making an unexpected comeback.

Japanese imaging and technology company Fujifilm Corp. has announced plans to increase its production capacity for magnetic-tape data storage media fivefold.

Because magnetic tape can be kept offline and stores data on a physical medium, it can serve as a secure backup largely beyond the reach of network-based cyberattacks.

In an age dominated by cloud computing, when so much data is stored online, one might have expected magnetic tape to disappear altogether. Instead, demand for Fujifilm’s storage media is reportedly soaring.

But cybersecurity was not the only consideration behind the Nordic countries’ efforts, legislative measures among them, to put the brakes on the wholesale shift toward cashless payments.

There was also a determination to protect the rights of consumers who cannot or simply prefer not to use credit cards or digital payment services to pay for life’s necessities with cash.

How far should we rely on technology, and for what purposes? What kind of society do we really want to live in?

The growing threat of cyberattacks gives us good reason to revisit these questions.

—The Asahi Shimbun, Oct. 30

articles.originalTitle: Названы необычные последствия новых выборов в США
articles.originalText: Промежуточные выборы в США, на которых изберут всю Палату представителей, треть Сената и 36 губернаторов из 50, окажут важное значение как для Демократической, так и Республиканской партий, включая их кандидатов в президенты 2028 года. Об этом сообщается в специальном аналитическом докладе агентства «Дубравский консалтинг», текст которого был предоставлен «Ленте.ру»
articles.originalFullText:
Промежуточные выборы в США, на которых изберут всю Палату представителей, треть Сената и 36 губернаторов из 50, окажут важное значение как для Демократической, так и Республиканской партий, включая их кандидатов в президенты 2028 года. Об этом сообщается в специальном аналитическом докладе агентства «Дубравский консалтинг», текст которого был предоставлен «Ленте.ру».

В частности, авторы обратили внимание на гонки за пост губернаторов штатов. Для США региональные выборы играют особую роль — лидеры штатов нередко умело сопротивляются президенту и его решениям, а для некоторых из них губернаторский пост может стать трамплином в Белый дом.

Одна из самых громких историй развернулась в Огайо. Эксперты относят этот штат к республиканским, но сентябрьский опрос дал демократке Эми Эктон 48 процентов, а ее оппоненту Вивеку Рамасвами только 45 процентов. Авторы доклада оценивают битву за этот штат как будущее Республиканской партии.

Ставки в Огайо высоки — этот штат стал «поставщиком» республиканцев нового типа, таких как вице-президент Вэнс. Итог голосования покажет, какая версия Республиканской партии победит: аппаратная или популистская

Еще одним эпицентром стал штат Флорида. Популярный губернатор-республиканец Рон Десантис построил персонализированную, наступательную систему власти. Если его преемник Байрон Дональдс победит, то это станет важным сигналом для Трампа — республиканцы могут насадить эту модель и в других штатах.

Губернаторская гонка повлияет и на облик Демократической партии. Губернатор Калифорнии Гэвин Ньюсом, которого многие считают будущим кандидатом в президенты, покидает свой пост. Демократы в штате ведут споры, какой курс надо выбрать в будущем: левый прогрессивный, технократический или умеренный. Исход выборов покажет, что именно хотят жители Калифорнии.

20 октября президент США Дональд Трамп заявил, что в случае победы демократов на промежуточных выборах в Конгресс Соединенные Штаты ждет судьба охваченной протестами Франции. Американский лидер подчеркнул, что не допустит подобного развития событий в США.

Промежуточные выборы в США, на которых изберут всю Палату представителей, треть Сената и 36 губернаторов из 50, окажут важное значение как для Демократической, так и Республиканской партий, включая их кандидатов в президенты 2028 года. Об этом сообщается в специальном аналитическом докладе агентства «Дубравский консалтинг», текст которого был предоставлен «Ленте.ру».

В частности, авторы обратили внимание на гонки за пост губернаторов штатов. Для США региональные выборы играют особую роль — лидеры штатов нередко умело сопротивляются президенту и его решениям, а для некоторых из них губернаторский пост может стать трамплином в Белый дом.

Одна из самых громких историй развернулась в Огайо. Эксперты относят этот штат к республиканским, но сентябрьский опрос дал демократке Эми Эктон 48 процентов, а ее оппоненту Вивеку Рамасвами только 45 процентов. Авторы доклада оценивают битву за этот штат как будущее Республиканской партии.

Ставки в Огайо высоки — этот штат стал «поставщиком» республиканцев нового типа, таких как вице-президент Вэнс. Итог голосования покажет, какая версия Республиканской партии победит: аппаратная или популистская

Еще одним эпицентром стал штат Флорида. Популярный губернатор-республиканец Рон Десантис построил персонализированную, наступательную систему власти. Если его преемник Байрон Дональдс победит, то это станет важным сигналом для Трампа — республиканцы могут насадить эту модель и в других штатах.

Губернаторская гонка повлияет и на облик Демократической партии. Губернатор Калифорнии Гэвин Ньюсом, которого многие считают будущим кандидатом в президенты, покидает свой пост. Демократы в штате ведут споры, какой курс надо выбрать в будущем: левый прогрессивный, технократический или умеренный. Исход выборов покажет, что именно хотят жители Калифорнии.

20 октября президент США Дональд Трамп заявил, что в случае победы демократов на промежуточных выборах в Конгресс Соединенные Штаты ждет судьба охваченной протестами Франции. Американский лидер подчеркнул, что не допустит подобного развития событий в США.

Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi has vowed to uphold Japan’s “exclusively defense-oriented” policy, as China continues to claim that Tokyo is “accelerating its remilitarization” with its defense buildup and shifting security policies.

Koizumi, speaking at an expanded meeting of Association of Southeast Asian Nations defense ministers on the Philippine island of Cebu late Thursday, said that Japan will set an example with its transparency as it revises its three key security documents — including its National Security Strategy — by the year-end.

The Japanese defense chief said the changes will improve his country’s ability to defend itself and contribute to the security of the region.

articles.originalTitle: Venezuela’s Rodríguez vows to hold election as Machado asks when
articles.originalText: Interim head of state Delcy Rodriguez and Maria Corina Machado are expected to vie for the presidency in a future election.
articles.originalFullText:
Venezuela’s acting president pledged to hold elections once the agency that oversees voting is overhauled, offering her most specific vision yet for restoring democracy even as the nation’s leading opposition figure pressed her to commit to a date next year.

The back-and-forth between the interim head of state Delcy Rodriguez and her challenger Maria Corina Machado in consecutive events was the closest thing to a direct confrontation the two have had since Machado returned from exile on Oct. 25. Both are expected to vie for the presidency in a future election.

“There will be elections, all those mandated by our constitution, organized by a renewed electoral authority and with the world as witness,” Rodriguez said in a rare televised address, shortly before Machado was due to make her first public remarks since her return.
articles.title: Родригес обещает провести выборы, когда Мачадо спросит
articles.text: Ожидается, что временный глава государства Делси Родригес и Мария Корина Мачадо будут бороться за пост президента на будущих выборах.
articles.fullText:
Исполняющий обязанности президента Венесуэлы пообещал провести выборы после того, как агентство, которое контролирует голосование, будет пересмотрено, предлагая свое самое конкретное видение восстановления демократии, даже когда ведущая оппозиционная фигура страны потребовала от нее назначить дату в следующем году.

Между временным главой государства Делси Родригесом и ее претенденткой Марией Кориной Мачадо в последовательных событиях было самое близкое к прямому противостоянию, которое они имели с тех пор, как Мачадо вернулся из изгнания 25 октября. Ожидается, что оба будут бороться за президентство на будущих выборах.

«Будут выборы, все те, которые предусмотрены нашей конституцией, организованы обновленной избирательной властью и со всем миром в качестве свидетеля», — сказала Родригес в редком телевизионном обращении, незадолго до того, как Мачадо должна была сделать свои первые публичные замечания после ее возвращения.

articles.originalTitle: Generative AI reduces working hours for government staff, survey finds
articles.originalText: Over 50% of the respondents said they were able to reduce working hours by at least one hour per week.
articles.originalFullText:
Employees at government ministries and agencies have been able to reduce their working hours by 110 minutes per week, on average, through the use of the Gennai generative artificial intelligence platform, a Digital Agency survey showed Friday.

The online survey was conducted among workers at the ministries and agencies in August and September, collecting valid responses from 6,439 people.

Over 50% of the respondents said they were able to reduce working hours by at least one hour per week.

Specifically, 35.1% said they cut working hours by one to three hours, 10.9% three to five hours, 5.2% five to 10 hours and 3.2% 10 hours or more. Meanwhile, 34.6% said their working hours remained largely the same.

Asked about the effects from the use of the AI platform, many said they were able to “quickly create a rough draft,” “find necessary information from vast volumes of documents” or “catch up with technical knowledge faster.”

The survey showed that 10.4% use the AI platform almost every day, 11% three or four times a week and 26.4% once or twice a week. A total of 31.2% said they rarely use or have never used it.

Gennai, developed and operated by the Digital Agency, is available to about 180,000 government employees and now features an AI agent function capable of autonomously performing two or more tasks simultaneously.
articles.fullText:
Сотрудники правительственных министерств и ведомств смогли сократить свое рабочее время в среднем на 110 минут в неделю за счет использования платформы генеративного искусственного интеллекта Gennai.

Онлайн-опрос проводился среди работников министерств и ведомств в августе и сентябре, собрав действительные ответы от 6439 человек.

Более 50% респондентов заявили, что смогли сократить рабочее время как минимум на один час в неделю.

В частности, 35,1% заявили, что они сократили рабочее время на один-три часа, 10,9% на три-пять часов, 5,2% на пять-10 часов и 3,2% на 10 часов и более. При этом 34,6% опрошенных заявили, что их рабочее время осталось прежним.

Отвечая на вопрос о последствиях использования платформы искусственного интеллекта, многие заявили, что им удалось «быстро создать черновой проект», «найти необходимую информацию из огромных объемов документов» или «быстрее получить технические знания».

Опрос показал, что 10,4% используют платформу ИИ почти каждый день, 11% три или четыре раза в неделю и 26,4% один или два раза в неделю. В общей сложности 31,2% сказали, что они редко используют или никогда не использовали его.

Gennai, разработанный и управляемый Digital Agency, доступен примерно 180 000 правительственных служащих и теперь имеет функцию агента ИИ, способную автономно выполнять две или более задач одновременно.

articles.originalTitle: Binance hit by $6.3 billion security breach in potential record crypto heist
articles.originalText: Binance said on Thursday that a security breach had affected an estimated $6.3 billion in assets, potentially making it the biggest cryptocurrency heist on record. The world's largest crypto exchange said it had recovered or frozen about $3 billion, while the incident sent Bitcoin and other digital currencies lower.
articles.originalFullText:
Binance said on Thursday that a security breach had affected an estimated $6.3 billion in assets, potentially making it the biggest cryptocurrency heist on record. The world's largest crypto exchange said it had recovered or frozen about $3 billion, while the incident sent Bitcoin and other digital currencies lower.

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever and might make investors rethink the risks of owning digital assets.

Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion as Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover "all hacking losses".

An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said.

Markets reacted immediately in early Asian trading on Friday.

Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.

Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8% while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading.

The incident could be the world's biggest crypto heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis and other industry experts.

"It's the biggest hack in history," said Aravind Srinivasan, head of large crypto market maker GSR's systematic OTC business.

Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure lately due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.

"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong.

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange's 2025 annual report.

"User funds remain safe," Binance said in a statement. "As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our security teams conduct checks, secure wallet infrastructure, and trace affected assets, with the close support of our law enforcement and industry partners."

Binance has secure asset fund

Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website.

"It's becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them," said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.

"My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn't cover a hack of meaningful size."

Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.

World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack. Binance's Yi said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.

Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties.

Incident adds to string of crypto thefts

Miguel Morel, CEO of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been hacked from Binance by an unknown actor.

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's vulnerability to hackers.

Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.

Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.

Coinbase said it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation.

In an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading after a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.

(FRANCE 24 with Reuters)
articles.fullText:
Binance заявила в четверг, что нарушение безопасности затронуло активы на сумму около 6,3 миллиарда долларов, что потенциально делает его крупнейшим ограблением криптовалюты. Крупнейшая в мире криптовалютная биржа заявила, что восстановила или заморозила около 3 миллиардов долларов, в то время как инцидент снизил биткойн и другие цифровые валюты.

Binance, крупнейшая в мире криптовалютная биржа, заявила, что нарушение безопасности привело к предполагаемому воздействию в 6,3 миллиарда долларов, которое, по мнению аналитиков, может составить самое большое крипто-хищение за всю историю и может заставить инвесторов переосмыслить риски владения цифровыми активами.

Binance заявила, что она работала с партнерами, чтобы заморозить затронутые активы, и на данный момент находится около 3 миллиардов долларов. Он не сообщил о состоянии оставшихся $3,3 млрд, поскольку соучредитель Binance И Хэ сказал, что компания покроет «все потери от взлома».

Первоначальное расследование показало, что взлом мог начаться с взломанного ноутбука, принадлежащего одному из его инженеров, который позволил злоумышленнику получить доступ к одной из его систем и сделать несанкционированный вывод средств.

Рынки отреагировали сразу на ранние азиатские торги в пятницу.

Биткоин упал более чем на 3% до шестинедельного минимума в $76 368, а эфир упал более чем на 3% до двухмесячного минимума в $2 178. BNB, токен, первоначально запущенный как Binance Coin, который можно использовать для оплаты сборов Binance, снизился на 5% за последние 24 часа до $709,70, согласно агрегатору рынка CoinGecko.

Акции криптобиржи Coinbase Global упали на 4,8%, в то время как акции Bitcoin Buyer Strategy упали почти на 6% в расширенной торговле в США.

Инцидент может стать крупнейшим в мире ограблением криптовалюты, считают аналитики Chainalysis и другие эксперты отрасли.

«Это самый большой взлом в истории», - сказал Аравинд Шринивасан, глава систематического внебиржевого бизнеса крупного производителя криптовалют GSR.

Помимо потенциальной потери активов, нарушение безопасности, вероятно, будет иметь более широкие последствия для криптовалют, которые в последнее время уже находились под давлением из-за более высоких процентных ставок в США и более мягкого спроса со стороны покупателей биржевых фондов, считают аналитики.

«Это может еще больше ослабить аппетит к риску и побудить инвесторов пересмотреть безопасность активов, хранящихся на централизованных биржах, а также риски платежеспособности и ликвидности», - сказал Тим Сунь, старший научный сотрудник HashKey Group, базирующейся в Гонконге.

Binance, которая позволяет пользователям покупать, продавать и торговать цифровыми активами, имеет 335 миллионов зарегистрированных пользователей по всему миру и имеет около 162,8 миллиарда долларов активов под стражей по состоянию на 2025 год.

«Пользовательские средства остаются в безопасности», — говорится в заявлении Binance. В качестве меры предосторожности все депозиты и снятие средств временно приостановлены, в то время как наши службы безопасности проводят проверки, обеспечивают безопасность инфраструктуры кошельков и отслеживают затронутые активы при тесной поддержке наших правоохранительных органов и отраслевых партнеров.

Binance имеет надежный фонд активов

Binance управляет фондом безопасных активов для пользователей, который является резервом, полностью хранящимся в биткойне, который предназначен для защиты активов пользователей в случаях нарушений безопасности.

«Стало очень трудно противостоять взломам, поскольку ИИ может найти уязвимости быстрее, чем вы можете их исправить», - сказал Бернардо Бритс, генеральный директор Trace Finance, компании по платежам и инфраструктуре стейблкоинов.

«Я считаю, что пользователи отойдут от небольших и средних бирж, (это) становится слишком рискованным, чтобы припарковать свои деньги где-то, что не может покрыть взлом значимого размера».

Эмитент Stablecoin Tether заявила, что заморозила активы, связанные с инцидентом, на сумму около 1,57 миллиарда долларов, а Circle заморозила более 800 миллионов долларов.

World Liberty Financial, криптокомпания, связанная с президентом США Дональдом Трампом и его семьей, заявила в четверг, что она работала с хранителем криптовалюты BitGo, чтобы заморозить средства, украденные в результате взлома Binance. Yi Binance заявила, что было заморожено 27 миллионов долларов в стейблкоинах и токены World Liberty на сумму около 2 миллионов долларов.

Криптовалютная фирма Ripple также заморозила около 200 миллионов долларов, сказал И. Джек Макдональд, старший вице-президент по стейблкоинам в Ripple, сказал, что компания внимательно следит за сообщениями о потенциальном эксплойте, связанном с Binance, и замораживает пострадавшие средства и координирует свои действия с соответствующими сторонами.

Инцидент добавил к строке крипто-краж

Мигель Морель, генеральный директор блокчейн-разведывательной фирмы Arkham, сказал, что данные указывают на то, что миллиарды долларов были взломаны Binance неизвестным актером.

Инцидент добавляет к череде криптовалютных краж. В прошлом году злоумышленники похитили криптовалюту на сумму 2,9 миллиарда долларов в результате почти 150 атак, по данным исследователей из TRM Labs. В сентябре криптовалютная биржа Bitget заявила, что с ее платформы было украдено около 350 миллионов долларов, что подчеркивает уязвимость отрасли для хакеров.

Организованные преступные группы все чаще используют криптовалюты для перемещения средств за пределы традиционной финансовой системы.

Binance.US, отдельная криптовалютная биржа, заявила, что на нее не повлиял инцидент с безопасностью.

Coinbase заявила, что не пострадала и следит за ситуацией.

В несвязанном инциденте ранее в четверг оператор рынка прогнозирования Polymarket временно приостановил торговлю после инцидента с безопасностью с участием стороннего поставщика. Позже компания возобновила торговлю и заявила, что полностью возместит убытки пострадавшим трейдерам.

(Франция 24 с Рейтер)

articles.originalFullText:
THE ASAHI SHIMBUN

October 30, 2026 at 12:44 JST

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announces plans on Oct. 29 to resume utility subsidies and wind down gasoline subsidies from December. (Takeshi Iwashita)

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced on Oct. 29 that Japan will begin gradually cutting gasoline subsidies in December, after reviving them this spring amid mounting tensions in the Middle East that drove up global oil prices.

Subsidies for electricity and gas bills will also resume in December and run through February.

Takaichi told reporters that the gasoline subsidy is “strictly an emergency measure to cushion the impact of sudden price changes,” adding that the government is “using more than 10 billion yen a day in precious taxpayer money to keep fuel prices down.”

The government currently subsidizes gasoline to keep the nationwide average price of regular gasoline at around 170 yen ($1.08) per liter. It will raise that benchmark by 5 yen each month toward early spring.

Takaichi said the government would consider the impact on people’s lives and economic activity, as well as crude oil prices, as it “moves smoothly toward a sustainable system.”

She declined to say how long the benchmark would continue to rise or when the subsidies would end, saying, “I don’t want to prejudge the matter.”

Launched in 2022, the gasoline subsidy program ended late last year when the former provisional gasoline tax rate was abolished. It was reinstated in March, with subsidies now exceeding 50 yen per liter.

Spending totaled about 9 trillion yen through September, at times reaching 300 billion yen a month.

The subsidies are funded through massive government contingency reserves, prompting concerns within the government and the ruling Liberal Democratic Party about the strain on public finances.

Takaichi instructed Economy Minister Ryosei Akazawa on Oct. 23 to review the program.

For electricity and gas bills, the government will provide subsidies of 1 yen per kilowatt-hour in December and 4.5 yen in January and February, saving a typical household about 7,000 yen over the three months.

The program will begin a month earlier than last winter, when subsidies ran from January through March. The government will decide on support measures for March based on weather conditions and energy prices.

Асахи Шимбун

30 октября 2026 в 12:44 JST

Премьер-министр Санаэ Такаичи объявил о планах 29 октября возобновить субсидии на коммунальные услуги и прекратить субсидии на бензин с декабря. (Такеши Ивашита)

29 октября премьер-министр Японии Санаэ Такаичи объявил, что Япония начнет постепенно сокращать субсидии на бензин в декабре, после того как весной этого года возобновит их на фоне растущей напряженности на Ближнем Востоке, которая привела к росту мировых цен на нефть.

Субсидии на счета за электроэнергию и газ возобновятся в декабре и будут действовать до февраля.

Такаичи сказал журналистам, что субсидия на бензин является «строго экстренной мерой, чтобы смягчить последствия внезапных изменений цен», добавив, что правительство «использует более 10 миллиардов иен в день в драгоценных деньгах налогоплательщиков, чтобы снизить цены на топливо».

В настоящее время правительство субсидирует бензин, чтобы сохранить среднюю цену обычного бензина в стране на уровне около 170 иен ($ 1,08) за литр. Это повысит этот ориентир на 5 иен каждый месяц к началу весны.

Такаичи сказал, что правительство рассмотрит влияние на жизнь людей и экономическую активность, а также цены на сырую нефть, поскольку она «плавно движется к устойчивой системе».

Она отказалась сказать, как долго эталон будет продолжать расти или когда субсидии закончатся, сказав: «Я не хочу предрешать этот вопрос».

Запущенная в 2022 году программа субсидирования бензина закончилась в конце прошлого года, когда была отменена бывшая временная ставка налога на бензин. Он был восстановлен в марте, а субсидии теперь превышают 50 иен за литр.

Расходы составили около 9 триллионов иен до сентября, иногда достигая 300 миллиардов иен в месяц.

Субсидии финансируются за счет огромных резервов правительства на случай непредвиденных обстоятельств, что вызывает обеспокоенность в правительстве и правящей Либерально-демократической партии по поводу нагрузки на государственные финансы.

Такаичи 23 октября поручил министру экономики Рёсею Аказаве пересмотреть программу.

Для счетов за электроэнергию и газ правительство предоставит субсидии в размере 1 иены за киловатт-час в декабре и 4,5 иены в январе и феврале, сэкономив типичному домохозяйству около 7 000 иен в течение трех месяцев.

Программа начнется на месяц раньше, чем прошлой зимой, когда субсидии шли с января по март. Правительство примет решение о мерах поддержки на март исходя из погодных условий и цен на энергоносители.

articles.originalTitle: Private-sector council proposes use of forex surplus to cover fiscal measures
articles.originalText: Funds are needed to cut the consumption tax rate on food to fight inflation, and to strengthen the country's defense capabilities.
articles.originalFullText:
Private-sector members of a key government council have proposed active use of surpluses in the state’s foreign exchange special account as financial resources to cover massive fiscal needs.

The proposal was presented at Thursday’s meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (CEFP), headed by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

CEFP members discussed concrete measures to thoroughly reform state budget compilation at a time when the government needs to secure a massive amount of funds for projects such as investments to make the country resilient and prosperous under the Takaichi administration’s growth strategy.

Funds are also needed for the government’s plans to cut the consumption tax rate on food from 8% to 1% for two years from April 2027 as a measure to fight inflation, and to strengthen the country’s defense capabilities.

In recent years, surpluses at the foreign exchange special account, which manages funds for currency market intervention, have reached about ¥5 trillion ($31.7 billion) annually thanks to increases in the yen value of foreign currency-denominated assets due to the depreciation of the Japanese currency, and in interest revenue reflecting higher interest rates overseas.

The Finance Ministry has a rule to set aside about 30% of such surpluses and transfer the rest to the government’s general and other accounts in principle in order to prevent fund shortages at the foreign exchange account because of factors such as rapid fluctuations in foreign exchange and interest rates.

The ministry sets aside surpluses so that the proportion of accumulated surpluses to government-held foreign assets stands at about 30%. At the end of fiscal 2024, the cumulative balance of surpluses stood at ¥30.2 trillion, with the proportion coming to 22.4%.

Private-sector members of the CEFP called on the government to adopt as a benchmark the difference between assets and debts including short-term government securities issued to raise yen funds for foreign exchange market intervention.

Given that the gap totaled ¥85.8 trillion at the end of fiscal 2024 and that the proportion to foreign currency-denominated assets topped 40%, the members stressed that sufficient fiscal buffers for foreign exchange-related risks have been secured for the time being based on the current exchange rate levels, urging the government to actively use surpluses at the foreign exchange special account.

On the compilation of the government’s fiscal 2027 budget, the private-sector members called for clarifying “as much as possible” not only budgetary measures for public-private investments for the first year but also the scale and time frame of fiscal measures, and specific ways of providing support for later years.

Члены ключевого правительственного совета частного сектора предложили активно использовать профициты на специальном валютном счете государства в качестве финансовых ресурсов для покрытия огромных финансовых потребностей.

Предложение было представлено на заседании Совета по экономической и фискальной политике (CEFP) во главе с премьер-министром Санаэ Такаичи.

Члены CEFP обсудили конкретные меры по тщательному реформированию составления государственного бюджета в то время, когда правительству необходимо обеспечить огромный объем средств для таких проектов, как инвестиции, чтобы сделать страну устойчивой и процветающей в соответствии со стратегией роста администрации Такаичи.

Средства также необходимы для планов правительства по снижению ставки налога на потребление продовольствия с 8% до 1% в течение двух лет с апреля 2027 года в качестве меры по борьбе с инфляцией и укреплению обороноспособности страны.

В последние годы профицит на специальном валютном счете, который управляет фондами для интервенции на валютном рынке, достиг около 5 триллионов иен (31,7 миллиарда долларов) ежегодно благодаря увеличению стоимости иен в активах, номинированных в иностранной валюте, из-за обесценивания японской валюты и в процентных доходах, отражающих более высокие процентные ставки за рубежом.

Министерство финансов имеет правило откладывать около 30% таких профицитов и переводить остальное на общие и другие счета правительства в принципе, чтобы предотвратить нехватку средств на валютном счете из-за таких факторов, как быстрые колебания валютных курсов и процентных ставок.

Министерство выделяет профициты, так что доля накопленных профицитов в иностранных активах, находящихся в ведении правительства, составляет около 30%. В конце финансового 2024 года совокупный баланс профицита составил 30,2 трлн иен, причем доля достигла 22,4%.

Члены CEFP призвали правительство принять в качестве ориентира разницу между активами и долгами, включая краткосрочные государственные ценные бумаги, выпущенные для привлечения средств иены для вмешательства на валютном рынке.

Учитывая, что на конец 2024 финансового года разрыв составил 85,8 трлн иен и что доля активов, номинированных в иностранной валюте, превысила 40%, члены подчеркнули, что на данный момент обеспечены достаточные фискальные буферы для рисков, связанных с иностранной валютой, на основе текущих уровней обменного курса, призвав правительство активно использовать профициты на специальном валютном счете.

При составлении бюджета правительства на 2027 финансовый год члены частного сектора призвали уточнить «насколько это возможно» не только бюджетные меры по государственно-частным инвестициям на первый год, но и масштаб и сроки фискальных мер, а также конкретные способы оказания поддержки на последующие годы.

articles.originalTitle: Dressing as a nurse this Halloween? Adding a red cross breaks the law.
articles.originalText: Often mistaken for a general symbol of medical care, the red cross is protected under the law and reserved for specific humanitarian purposes.
articles.originalFullText:
As Halloween revelers prepare to take to the streets in nurse uniforms and other costumes, the Japanese Red Cross Society is warning that using the iconic red cross emblem without authorization is against the law — even as a costume accessory.

The emblem, often mistaken for a general symbol of medical care, is protected under international and domestic laws and is reserved for specific humanitarian purposes.

The Red Cross emblem was established under the Geneva Conventions to identify people and facilities that must not be attacked during armed conflicts. Japan’s law on the Red Cross emblem also prohibits anyone other than the Japanese Red Cross Society and those authorized by it from using the symbol without permission. Violators face up to six months in prison or a fine of up to ¥300,000 ($1,900).

“The Red Cross emblem is not a symbol of medical care. It is a last lifeline in times of emergency,” said Akihiko Saito, an official at the Japanese Red Cross Society.

The organization warns that casual use of the emblem during peacetime could undermine its significance when it is needed most. Since 2022, the organization has issued annual reminders on social media around Halloween urging people not to use the symbol on costumes or accessories.

The emblem is not limited to a specific color or cross shape. This is intended to prevent people or facilities from being attacked simply because they cannot reproduce the exact design amid the confusion of armed conflict.

Similar symbols are also prohibited, including crosses in shades of red such as pink and crosses of varying shapes. The organization cautions that people should also avoid using the emblem on nurse uniforms, caps and even medicine boxes.

MalyMoon, a cosplay costume retailer with stores in Tokyo’s Akihabara district and Shanghai, offers 40 types of nurse costumes for this year’s Halloween. The company uses heart motifs and accessories such as toy syringes to evoke the look without using the Red Cross emblem.

“We were aware that using the red cross emblem was prohibited, but the Japanese Red Cross Society’s warning has reminded us to be even more careful,” an official at a company operating the store said.

В то время как празднующие Хэллоуин готовятся выйти на улицы в форме медсестер и других костюмах, Японское общество Красного Креста предупреждает, что использование знаковой эмблемы красного креста без разрешения противоречит закону — даже в качестве аксессуара для костюма.

Эмблема, часто принимаемая за общий символ медицинской помощи, защищена международным и внутренним законодательством и зарезервирована для конкретных гуманитарных целей.

Эмблема Красного Креста была создана в соответствии с Женевскими конвенциями для идентификации людей и объектов, которые не должны подвергаться нападениям во время вооруженных конфликтов. Японский закон об эмблеме Красного Креста также запрещает любому, кроме Японского общества Красного Креста и лиц, уполномоченных им, использовать символ без разрешения. Нарушителям грозит до шести месяцев тюрьмы или штраф до 300 000 иен ($1 900).

Эмблема Красного Креста не является символом медицинской помощи. Это последний спасательный круг во время чрезвычайной ситуации, - сказал Акихико Сайто, представитель Японского общества Красного Креста.

Организация предупреждает, что случайное использование эмблемы в мирное время может подорвать ее значение, когда она больше всего нужна. С 2022 года организация выпускает ежегодные напоминания в социальных сетях о Хэллоуине, призывающие людей не использовать символ на костюмах или аксессуарах.

Эмблема не ограничивается определенным цветом или формой креста. Это призвано предотвратить нападения на людей или объекты просто потому, что они не могут воспроизвести точную конструкцию в условиях путаницы вооруженного конфликта.

Подобные символы также запрещены, включая кресты в оттенках красного, такие как розовый и кресты различной формы. Организация предупреждает, что люди также должны избегать использования эмблемы на униформе медсестры, кепках и даже коробках с лекарствами.

MalyMoon, магазин косплейных костюмов в токийском районе Акихабара и Шанхае, предлагает 40 видов костюмов медсестер на Хэллоуин в этом году. Компания использует сердечные мотивы и аксессуары, такие как игрушечные шприцы, чтобы вызвать внешний вид без использования эмблемы Красного Креста.

«Мы знали, что использование эмблемы красного креста было запрещено, но предупреждение Японского общества Красного Креста напомнило нам о том, что нужно быть еще более осторожными», — сказал представитель компании.

articles.originalTitle: Africa making Olympic debut with 2026 Dakar Youth Games
articles.originalText: Senegal is the first African country to host an Olympic sporting event.
articles.originalFullText:
Dakar – The first Olympic sporting event to ever be held in Africa has been a long time in the making but the Dakar Youth Olympics are ready to deliver despite a four-year postponement, International Olympic Committee President Kirsty Coventry said on Thursday.

Senegal is the first African country to host an Olympic sporting event, with the Youth Games opening on Saturday with the participation of almost 2,700 athletes, aged 14 to 17, from 204 national Olympic committees.

The Games, which will run until Nov. 13, were initially set for 2022 but had to be postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

“It’s here,“ Coventry told a news conference in Dakar after inspecting the venues and the athletes’ village ahead of Saturday’s opening ceremony. “We are so happy. This has been a long time in the making. We have gotten all the big milestones under way.”

Coventry, a former Olympic swimming champion from Zimbabwe, is the first African to lead the organization, having been elected in 2025.

Dakar Games organizers said they had to deal with last-minute energy and rain issues but have given the green light for the start with more than 6,000 volunteers helping in the organization.

Security will also be considerable and will include Spanish and French police officers, with experience from the 2024 Paris Olympics, organizers said.

“The team can give all assurances that everyone is ready to go,“ Coventry said. “I specifically feel very proud. I was part of the IOC when we took the decision (to award the Games to Dakar). To finally be here it feels like a long time coming ... and to see the level of an Olympic event being displayed.”

Humphrey Kayange, the IOC’s coordination commission chair for the Games, said the impact of the Youth Games could be wider.

Africa has never hosted the Summer Olympics despite bids from several countries in the past. On Thursday Durban was named as South Africa’s candidate for either the 2036 or 2040 Olympics.

“Seeing it (Dakar) come together has been great,” Kayange said. “What it leaves behind is legacy, infrastructure, venues, personnel. We hope the ripple effect does not die. There is a lot of potential and opportunity for it to be a shining start.”

Дакар - Первое олимпийское спортивное мероприятие, которое когда-либо проводилось в Африке, было давно готово, но молодежные Олимпийские игры в Дакаре готовы провести, несмотря на четырехлетнюю отсрочку, заявил президент Международного олимпийского комитета Кирсти Ковентри.

Сенегал является первой африканской страной, которая примет олимпийское спортивное мероприятие, с открытием Молодежных игр в субботу с участием почти 2700 спортсменов в возрасте от 14 до 17 лет из 204 национальных олимпийских комитетов.

Игры, которые продлятся до 13 ноября, изначально были назначены на 2022 год, но пришлось отложить из-за пандемии COVID-19.

«Это здесь», — сказал Ковентри на пресс-конференции в Дакаре после осмотра мест проведения соревнований и деревни спортсменов в преддверии церемонии открытия. "Мы так счастливы. Это было долгое время в разработке. Мы уже приступили к выполнению всех важных задач».

Ковентри, бывший олимпийский чемпион по плаванию из Зимбабве, является первым африканцем, который возглавит организацию, будучи избранным в 2025 году.

Организаторы Игр в Дакаре заявили, что в последнюю минуту им пришлось столкнуться с проблемами с энергией и дождями, но дали зеленый свет для начала более 6000 добровольцев, помогающих организации.

Безопасность также будет значительной и будет включать испанских и французских полицейских, имеющих опыт проведения Олимпийских игр в Париже в 2024 году.

«Команда может дать все гарантии, что все готовы идти», — сказал Ковентри. "Я особенно горжусь этим. Я был частью МОК, когда мы приняли решение (присудить Игры Дакару). Чтобы наконец-то оказаться здесь, кажется, что наступает время... и увидеть, как отображается уровень олимпийского события».

Хамфри Каянге, председатель координационной комиссии МОК по Играм, сказал, что влияние Молодежных игр может быть шире.

Африка никогда не принимала Летние Олимпийские игры, несмотря на заявки от нескольких стран в прошлом. В четверг Дурбан был назван кандидатом Южной Африки на Олимпийские игры 2036 или 2040 годов.

«Увидеть, как они сближаются, было здорово», — сказал Каянге. «То, что он оставляет, — это наследие, инфраструктура, места проведения, персонал. Мы надеемся, что эффект ряби не умрет. Существует большой потенциал и возможность для того, чтобы это стало блестящим началом».

articles.originalTitle: Bank of Japan holds rates steady even as inflation ticks up
articles.originalText: Consumer prices are rising more than 2% a year, a rate that the bank has said is its target.
articles.originalFullText:
The Bank of Japan held rates steady even as inflation ticks up again and is now above the central bank’s target rate for core consumer price increases.

It kept its policy rate — the uncollateralized overnight call rate — at 1.25%, as it concluded a two-day policy meeting on Friday.

Given that the last move higher was just in September, analysts and investors widely expected that the bank would sit tight this time.

The BOJ also released its quarterly report on the economy and prices on Friday, and the report indicated that underlying inflation in Japan has reached the bank’s 2% target. The BOJ has said its job from now on is to anchor inflation at that level.

The 2% inflation target was first introduced in 2013, under the leadership of then-Gov. Haruhiko Kuroda, Gov. Kazuo Ueda’s predecessor. At the time, Kuroda pledged to achieve the 2% target in two years, but it eventually took 13 years to get there.

Japan’s headline inflation stayed above 2% for 45 consecutive months between April 2022 and December 2025, but the BOJ maintained that underlying inflation — which excludes price movements that might be temporary — remained below 2%.

Inflation topped 2% in Japan for the first time this year in September, according to government data released last week. The data showed that consumer prices rose 2.1% year over year that month.

Inflation excluding volatile fresh food also stood at 2.1%, the highest since December last year and matching a forecast by analysts. The reading excluding both fresh food and energy was 2.4%.

Ueda is scheduled to give a news conference later on Friday.
